# Conventions guide

How I structure, write, test and document Python and ML projects. These are the rules every repo follows; the
`conventions` Claude Code plugin carries them to Claude, one skill per area, and the `conventions-hooks` package checks
what a tool can.

Version 0.1.0 · last reviewed 2026-11-05 · owner: nuinashco

- [How to read](#how-to-read) · [Where the other rules live](#where-the-other-rules-live) · [Retired rules](#retired-rules) · [Quick reference](#quick-reference)

## How to read

- **MUST**, **SHOULD** and **MAY** follow [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) as clarified by
  [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174): they carry their meaning only in capitals.
  - **MUST**: checked by a tool or test where possible. A justified exception gets a comment at the site naming the
    rule (`# noqa: BLE001 - a failing callback must not stop training`, or
    `# conventions: TYP-4 - the base class from httpx needs __init__.` for `check-conventions`).
  - **SHOULD**: the default. Deviate when you can say why.
  - **MAY**: a matter of taste, written down so it is consistent.
- Every rule has an ID (`STY-4`) for reviews and commit bodies, a *Why*, and a *Check*: a ruff rule, pyright, a hook
  of this repo, a test, `template` when [nuinashco/rnd-template](https://github.com/nuinashco/rnd-template) sets it
  up, or `review` when no tool can tell. [COVERAGE.md](COVERAGE.md) lists the MUST rules only review checks.
- Rules apply to every project unless tagged **[rnd]** (research and development: tools, pipelines, training).
- A repo that can't follow a rule yet lists it under "Deviations" in its CONTRIBUTING.md, with the reason. A rule that
  does not apply to the repo at all goes in `ignore` of its `[tool.conventions]` table (TOOL-4), and the hooks skip it.
- Changing a rule means editing it under `rules/` in nuinashco/conventions, regenerating this file and the plugin with
  `make build`, and changing the checks and templates it affects in the same commit, then tagging a new version.
  Projects pick it up through the plugin and by upgrading `conventions-hooks`.

## Where the other rules live

The IDs below belong to the repos that implement them, with the same shape.

| rules | repo | about |

| FAM-1 to FAM-5, CFG-1 to CFG-8, ERR-1, ERR-2, LOG-1, LOG-3, RUN-1, RUN-2 | [nuinashco/nuikit](https://github.com/nuinashco/nuikit/blob/main/docs/guide.md) | the shared library: families, configs, errors, logging, run directories, seeding |
| LAY-4, LAY-7, ENV-1 to ENV-3, TST-5, RUN-3 to RUN-7, TOOL-3 | [nuinashco/rnd-template](https://github.com/nuinashco/rnd-template) | the project template: top-level layout, entry points, paths, invariant tests, reproducibility and data, `copier update` |

## Retired rules

IDs are never reused.

- GIT-4, retired on 2026-10-19: commit messages are one line, without trailers (GIT-2).
- UNI-1 to UNI-6, retired on 2026-11-05 with the uni course profile.

## Quick reference

| rule | level | summary |
|---|---|---|
| [LAY-1](#lay-1-must) | MUST | Projects use uv with the `uv_build` backend, the src layout and a committed `uv.lock`. |
| [LAY-2](#lay-2-must) | MUST | A distribution has one top-level import package, `src/<pkg>/`. A standalone part of the project (a proxy, a client) is a subpackage such as `<pkg>/proxy/`, isolated by an import contract (ARC-1). |
| [LAY-3](#lay-3-must) | MUST | `requires-python` starts at the latest stable CPython when the project is created (3.14 as of 2026-10). Pin lower only when a dependency or runtime forces it, and say which one in a comment next to the pin. |
| [LAY-5](#lay-5-should) | SHOULD | Developer tools go in `[dependency-groups] dev`. Heavy optional features (GPU backends, trackers) are extras, and their imports are lazy (ARC-8). |
| [LAY-6](#lay-6-must) | MUST | A Makefile runs every routine task and documents itself: `make help` lists the targets from their `##` comments. The standard targets are `setup lint format typecheck test check`, plus what the project needs, such as `test-integration` and `configs` in an rnd project or `build` in a library. |
| [ARC-1](#arc-1-must-rnd) | MUST [rnd] | Dependencies between a package's subpackages point one way, and the direction is declared as import-linter contracts in `pyproject.toml`. A `layers` contract orders the subpackages from the entry points down to the lowest layer (such as `paths`), and it is exhaustive, so a new subpackage fails `make check` until it is placed in a layer. |
| [ARC-2](#arc-2-must) | MUST | Every seam has a pure half that decides and an effectful half that acts: `plan.py` / `served.py`, `adapter.py` / `runner.py`, `compiler.py` / `harness.py`. |
| [ARC-3](#arc-3-must) | MUST | Each entry point has one composition root, where objects are built and wired: the `cli/<command>.py` function, or the script itself. |
| [ARC-4](#arc-4-must) | MUST | Code branches on declared capabilities, not identities. Use a `ClassVar[bool]` such as `requires_hardware`, or a method that returns `None` when a feature is absent; never `if item.kind == "api"` or `isinstance(x, ConcreteItem)`. |
| [ARC-5](#arc-5-should) | SHOULD | Split the top level by domain (`evaluation/`, `grading/`, `endpoints/`) and split inside a domain by role. |
| [ARC-6](#arc-6-should) | SHOULD | Abstract on the third repetition, not the second. Until then prefer duplication: "duplication is far cheaper than the wrong abstraction" ([Metz](https://sandimetz.com/blog/2016/1/20/the-wrong-abstraction)). |
| [ARC-7](#arc-7-should) | SHOULD | Use modules as namespaces: `from <pkg>.evaluation import harness`, then `harness.run(...)`. Write a class only when there is state or polymorphism; otherwise write functions. |
| [ARC-8](#arc-8-must) | MUST | Heavy or optional third-party modules (torch, vllm, litellm, cloud SDKs, wandb) are imported inside the function that needs them. Annotations that name them use `if TYPE_CHECKING:` imports. |
| [TYP-1](#typ-1-must) | MUST | Every function signature in `src/` is annotated; test functions and fixtures may skip annotations. pyright in standard mode passes on `src/` and `tests/`, and strict mode passes on the `src/` of a library other repos import, such as nuikit. |
| [TYP-2](#typ-2-must) | MUST | Use modern syntax: `X \| None`, builtin generics, `collections.abc` for abstract containers, PEP 695 generics and `type` aliases. |
| [TYP-3](#typ-3-must) | MUST | While `requires-python` is below 3.14, every module starts with `from __future__ import annotations`. From 3.14 on it is never used: [PEP 649](https://peps.python.org/pep-0649/) makes annotations lazy, and [PEP 749](https://peps.python.org/pep-0749/) schedules the import for deprecation. |
| [TYP-4](#typ-4-must) | MUST | pydantic is only for data parsed from outside: configs, HTTP bodies, files. Every other class is an attrs class: `@frozen` for values, `@define` for stateful objects, family bases and items included. |
| [TYP-5](#typ-5-must) | MUST | Mind three attrs behaviours, each verified on attrs 26.1: `@define` builds a new class, so a registering decorator must be the outermost one ([FAM-2](https://github.com/nuinashco/nuikit/blob/main/docs/guide.md#fam-2-must)); `__init_subclass__` runs twice for slotted classes, so hooks in it must be idempotent; Slots stop attribute typos only when every base class is slotted, which is why family bases are attrs classes too. |
| [TYP-6](#typ-6-must) | MUST | Family bases are ABCs: the registry checks subclassing, and items inherit `Config` and helpers. An injected collaborator that only needs a shape (a clock, an HTTP client, an uploader) is typed as a `Protocol`, so fakes need no inheritance. |
| [TYP-7](#typ-7-should) | SHOULD | Use `Literal` for small closed sets of config values, and `StrEnum` when code iterates over the set or attaches behaviour to it. |
| [TYP-8](#typ-8-should) | SHOULD | Avoid `Any` outside JSON-shaped payloads and lazily imported third-party objects. Use `object` for "accepts anything". |
| [TYP-9](#typ-9-must) | MUST | Dicts are for wire payloads only (JSON in, JSON out). A dict with a fixed set of known keys is a class. |
| [STY-1](#sty-1-must) | MUST | Format with ruff format: 88 columns, double quotes. |
| [STY-2](#sty-2-must) | MUST | Lint with the template's curated rule set: `E F W I B UP SIM RET PTH C4 RUF TID FBT N PERF G LOG BLE PL D NPY ERA T20 C90` (plus `FA` below 3.14). |
| [STY-3](#sty-3-must) | MUST | Imports are absolute. |
| [STY-4](#sty-4-must) | MUST | Every optional parameter and every boolean parameter is keyword-only (after `*`). Only the one or two obvious subjects of a call are positional. |
| [STY-5](#sty-5-must) | MUST | Naming: Modules are short nouns (`harness`, `soundness`). Functions are verbs (`select`, `bind`); Classes are nouns, and family items carry the family suffix (`LiteLLMEndpoint`, `GoldPatches`); Schemas end in `Config`. Acronyms stay capitalised (`HDBSCANClustering`, `BQ2GCSCollector`); Constants are UPPER_SNAKE right after the imports; Anything not used outside its module starts with `_`. |
| [STY-6](#sty-6-must) | MUST | A name holding a number with a unit ends in a short unit suffix: `_s`, `_ms`, `_mb`, `_gb`, `_tokens`, `_steps`. |
| [STY-7](#sty-7-must) | MUST | Use pathlib, never `os.path`. |
| [STY-8](#sty-8-must) | MUST | `.py` files are ASCII: use `;`, `:`, `-` and `->`, never em dashes or Unicode arrows. Markdown may use any typography. |
| [STY-9](#sty-9-should) | SHOULD | Prefer early returns to nesting, comprehensions to `map`/`filter`, and `match` for dispatch on a shape or a file suffix. |
| [STY-10](#sty-10-should) | SHOULD | Keep within the complexity budget (C901 at 10, pylint's branch and statement limits). Split long functions at real seams, not into one-call helpers that are shallow modules ([Ousterhout](https://github.com/johnousterhout/aposd-vs-clean-code)). |
| [DOC-1](#doc-1-must) | MUST | Every module starts with a one-line docstring stating its single responsibility. A CLI module's or script's docstring is its `--help` text and may add a usage block. |
| [DOC-2](#doc-2-must) | MUST | Docstrings are one line where possible: a function's is imperative ("Return the run directory for `name`."); `D401` checks this; a class's is a noun phrase saying what an instance represents ("Spacing between requests to one upstream."); every public class has one (`D101`); a function or method gets one when its name and signature don't already say it all. |
| [DOC-3](#doc-3-should) | SHOULD | Add Google-style `Args:`, `Returns:` or `Raises:` sections only for what types can't express: units, shapes, valid ranges, what `None` or an empty value means, and errors that are part of the contract. |
| [DOC-4](#doc-4-must) | MUST | A comment explains what the code can't say: an external constraint; a non-obvious reason; a unit; where a value came from (cite the source); what `None` means. |
| [DOC-5](#doc-5-must) | MUST | Comments are sentences: capitalised and ending with a period. A sentence that opens with a lowercase name puts it in backticks (`` `git` is not installed. ``). |
| [DOC-6](#doc-6-should) | SHOULD | A `TODO` says why it isn't done now. Code generated without review is marked as such until reviewed. |
| [DOC-7](#doc-7-must) | MUST | A YAML comment, and so a `Field` description that a mirror turns into one ([CFG-3](https://github.com/nuinashco/nuikit/blob/main/docs/guide.md#cfg-3-must)), lists a setting's options (`auto\|console\|json`) or says what its key and value can't: a unit the name lacks, what `null` or an edge value means, a side effect, a source. |
| [ERR-3](#err-3-must) | MUST | A message is lowercase with no trailing period. It states what is wrong, then `; ` and the remedy, naming the command or config key. |
| [ERR-4](#err-4-must) | MUST | Fail fast at the edge: check that paths exist, kinds are registered and credentials work (a one-token ping) before any expensive work starts. |
| [ERR-5](#err-5-must) | MUST | Translating an exception uses `raise ... from err`. A broad `except Exception` exists only at an isolation point, such as a callback that must not stop training or a best-effort notification, and its `noqa` says why. |
| [ERR-6](#err-6-may) | MAY | Messages are written at the raise site. Ruff's TRY003 and EM rules, which want them inside the class, are not selected. |
| [LOG-2](#log-2-must) | MUST | Events are stable snake_case ids with key-value context: `log.info("proxy_started", port=8000)`. Never build an event with an f-string or `%`. |
| [LOG-4](#log-4-must) | MUST | Logs record events. Output meant for the user (tables, results) goes to stdout through `click.echo` or rich, never through the logger. |
| [LOG-5](#log-5-should) | SHOULD | Bind run context once with `structlog.contextvars.bind_contextvars(run=...)` instead of repeating it in every event. |
| [TST-1](#tst-1-must) | MUST | Tests are pytest functions (no test classes) named as sentences stating a behaviour: `test_sound_selection_never_falls_back_to_every_task`. |
| [TST-2](#tst-2-must) | MUST | Unit tests come first. Each case covers a distinct branch or behaviour: no cross-product parametrisation, and nothing re-tested at a higher level that a unit test already covers. |
| [TST-3](#tst-3-must) | MUST | Test doubles are in-process fakes (`ScriptedEndpoint`, `httpx.MockTransport`), `tmp_path` and `monkeypatch`. `unittest.mock` is banned. Fakes live in `tests/conftest.py` or `tests/fakes.py`; a fake with logic has its own tests. |
| [TST-4](#tst-4-must) | MUST | The layout mirrors `src/` module by module: `tests/<pkg>/<sub>/test_<module>.py` for every module with branching logic. Exempt modules are those with nothing a unit test could distinguish: schemas whose rules pydantic enforces, error classes, re-exporting `__init__` files, and thin wrappers that only start an external process (a `docker build`). |
| [TST-6](#tst-6-must) | MUST | Child processes, servers and Docker appear only in tests of what can't be measured in process. Before adding a slow test, check `pytest --durations=10`. |
| [TST-7](#tst-7-should) | SHOULD | Separate arrange, act and assert with blank lines. Compare related values in one tuple assert. A test module's docstring states the invariant it protects. |
| [TST-8](#tst-8-should) | SHOULD | Test ML code with tiny real models, not mocks: loss decreases, and a batch can be overfitted ([Yan](https://eugeneyan.com/writing/unit-testing-ml/)). |
| [RDOC-1](#rdoc-1-must) | MUST | README.md is the user's and operator's view: setup, daily workflow, commands, outputs, caveats. CONTRIBUTING.md is the contributor's view: architecture, layout, families, configs, deviations, the "Extending" table, tests and commits. |
| [RDOC-2](#rdoc-2-must) | MUST | A standalone subpackage has its own README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md next to its code. |
| [RDOC-3](#rdoc-3-must) | MUST | Diagrams are mermaid. Flowcharts colour pure components with `classDef pure` and effectful ones with `classDef side`, using the template's palette. |
| [RDOC-4](#rdoc-4-must) | MUST | AGENTS.md is the entry point for coding agents, at most 60 lines: commands, layout, what this repo asks beyond the conventions, and pointers to CONTRIBUTING. |
| [RDOC-5](#rdoc-5-must) | MUST | Docs change in the same commit as the code they describe. A stale doc is a bug. |
| [GIT-1](#git-1-must) | MUST | Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/): a standard type: `feat fix docs refactor test build ci perf style chore revert`; an optional scope; a lowercase imperative subject, with no period, of at most 72 characters; no articles (`a`, `an`, `the`) and no filler: say what changed in as few words as hold it. |
| [GIT-2](#git-2-must) | MUST | A commit message is one line: no body and no trailers. A reason worth keeping goes where readers look for it: a code comment for a constraint, the PR description for an alternative that was rejected. |
| [GIT-3](#git-3-must) | MUST | Branches are short-lived and named `<type>/<slug>` (`feat/`, `fix/`, `docs/`, `refactor/`, plus `exp/` for experiments). Merges are squash-merges, and the PR title is the conventional commit that lands on `main`. |
| [GIT-5](#git-5-must) | MUST | Secrets, data, run outputs and notebook outputs are never committed. |
| [GIT-6](#git-6-must) | MUST | A PR description follows `.github/pull_request_template.md`: a summary of why, the changes made with the alternatives rejected, and the checklist; results, how to reproduce them and notes for the reviewer when they apply. |
| [TOOL-1](#tool-1-must) | MUST | `make check` runs ruff check, ruff format `--check`, pyright, `lint-imports` and pytest, and CI runs it on every pull request. |
| [TOOL-2](#tool-2-must) | MUST | Tool versions come from `uv.lock`. Hooks for Python tools are local `uv run` hooks, so pre-commit, CI and editors all use the same versions. |
| [TOOL-4](#tool-4-must) | MUST | The checks this guide adds on top of ruff are the `conventions-hooks` package of nuinashco/conventions. A repo opts in with a `[tool.conventions]` table in its root `pyproject.toml`, where `ignore = ["STY-4"]` turns rules off for that repo, and adds the package as a dev dependency pinned by `uv.lock`. |
| [TOOL-5](#tool-5-must) | MUST | Files nobody edits by hand are listed in `.gitattributes` with `protected=<why>`: `generated`: config mirrors, `.copier-answers.yml`, and whatever a build step writes; `vendored`: code copied in from another repo and changed only there; `published`: third-party files kept as published, such as `notebooks/reference/`. |
| [TOOL-6](#tool-6-should) | SHOULD | A check that asks an LLM, such as a `claude -p` hook or a review subagent, is a judge and is built as one: narrow criteria with named verdicts, an "unsure" outcome instead of a guess, a cited line for every finding, a fresh context holding only the artefact and the rules, and structured output wherever code reads the verdict. |

## 1. Layout and packaging (LAY)

Which top-level folders a project has (LAY-4) and where its entry points live (LAY-7) are rules of
[nuinashco/rnd-template](https://github.com/nuinashco/rnd-template).

### LAY-1 MUST

Projects use uv with the `uv_build` backend, the src layout and a committed `uv.lock`.

*Why:* tests then run against the package as installed, not against the working tree
([Hynek](https://hynek.me/articles/testing-packaging/), [pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/explanation/goodpractices.html));
`uv init` generates this layout by default.

*Check:* template.

### LAY-2 MUST

A distribution has one top-level import package, `src/<pkg>/`. A standalone part of the project (a proxy, a client) is
a subpackage such as `<pkg>/proxy/`, isolated by an import contract (ARC-1). There is no `utils/`, `common/`, `core/`
or `helpers/` grab bag: each module is named after its one responsibility. Extract a part into its own distribution
only when a second repo depends on it.

*Why:* uv supports several top-level modules but ["does not recommend this
structure"](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/build-backend/) because generic names like `common` collide in
site-packages; a distinctive name avoids that.

*Check:* `module-name = "<pkg>"` in the template; `check-conventions` flags grab-bag module names under `src/`.

### LAY-3 MUST

`requires-python` starts at the latest stable CPython when the project is created (3.14 as of 2026-10). Pin lower only
when a dependency or runtime forces it, and say which one in a comment next to the pin. A pre-release dependency is
acceptable when it is the first to support that Python, with the reason next to it: nuikit needs
`hydra-core>=1.4.0rc1` because 1.3.x crashes on 3.14.

*Check:* template default; review.

### LAY-5 SHOULD

Developer tools go in `[dependency-groups] dev`. Heavy optional features (GPU backends, trackers) are extras, and their
imports are lazy (ARC-8).

*Check:* review.

### LAY-6 MUST

A Makefile runs every routine task and documents itself: `make help` lists the targets from their `##` comments. The
standard targets are `setup lint format typecheck test check`, plus what the project needs, such as
`test-integration` and `configs` in an rnd project or `build` in a library.

*Why:* one memorable entry point for people, CI and agents.

*Check:* template.

## 2. Architecture (ARC)

### ARC-1 MUST [rnd]

Dependencies between a package's subpackages point one way, and the direction is declared as import-linter contracts
in `pyproject.toml`. A `layers` contract orders the subpackages from the entry points down to the lowest layer (such as
`paths`), and it is exhaustive, so a new subpackage fails `make check` until it is placed in a layer. A standalone
subpackage never imports the rest of the package except the lowest layer, and an explicit `forbidden` contract says
so, whatever layer it sits in. CONTRIBUTING draws the project's own layers.

*Why:* a module hides a design decision
([Parnas 1972](https://blog.acolyer.org/2016/09/05/on-the-criteria-to-be-used-in-decomposing-systems-into-modules/)).
Python has no package-private visibility, so a checked contract is the only way to keep a boundary
([Brown](https://simonbrown.je/modular-monolith)).

*Check:* `lint-imports` in `make check`.

### ARC-2 MUST

Every seam has a pure half that decides and an effectful half that acts: `plan.py` / `served.py`, `adapter.py` /
`runner.py`, `compiler.py` / `harness.py`. A dry run executes the pure half for real and logs what the effectful half
would do.

*Why:* functional core, imperative shell
([Bernhardt](https://www.destroyallsoftware.com/screencasts/catalog/functional-core-imperative-shell)). The pure half is
unit-tested without doubles, and the effectful half stays thin.

*Check:* review. CONTRIBUTING diagrams colour the two halves (RDOC-3).

### ARC-3 MUST

Each entry point has one composition root, where objects are built and wired: the `cli/<command>.py` function, or the
script itself. Everything else receives collaborators through constructor arguments. Module-level state is limited to
loggers, path constants and family registries.

*Why:* explicit dependencies replace patching in tests
([Cosmic Python ch. 13](https://www.cosmicpython.com/book/chapter_13_dependency_injection.html)).

*Check:* review.

### ARC-4 MUST

Code branches on declared capabilities, not identities. Use a `ClassVar[bool]` such as `requires_hardware`, or a method
that returns `None` when a feature is absent; never `if item.kind == "api"` or `isinstance(x, ConcreteItem)`.

*Why:* adding an item never edits its callers.

*Check:* `check-conventions` flags comparisons with a `kind` attribute; review for `isinstance`.

### ARC-5 SHOULD

Split the top level by domain (`evaluation/`, `grading/`, `endpoints/`) and split inside a domain by role.

*Why:* layers at the top level suit only small systems
([Fowler](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/PresentationDomainDataLayering.html)).

*Check:* review.

### ARC-6 SHOULD

Abstract on the third repetition, not the second. Until then prefer duplication: "duplication is far cheaper than the
wrong abstraction" ([Metz](https://sandimetz.com/blog/2016/1/20/the-wrong-abstraction)).

*Check:* review.

### ARC-7 SHOULD

Use modules as namespaces: `from <pkg>.evaluation import harness`, then `harness.run(...)`. Write a class only when
there is state or polymorphism; otherwise write functions.

*Check:* review.

### ARC-8 MUST

Heavy or optional third-party modules (torch, vllm, litellm, cloud SDKs, wandb) are imported inside the function that
needs them. Annotations that name them use `if TYPE_CHECKING:` imports.

*Why:* CLI start-up time, test runtime, and optional extras.

*Check:* `check-conventions` flags a module-level import of a known heavy module under `src/`; review for the others;
ruff PLC0415 is off on purpose.

## 3. Types and data (TYP)

### TYP-1 MUST

Every function signature in `src/` is annotated; test functions and fixtures may skip annotations. pyright in standard
mode passes on `src/` and `tests/`, and strict mode passes on the `src/` of a library other repos import, such as
nuikit.

*Why:* the code relies on types (generics, `ClassVar`, `Config` bindings) that only a checker verifies.

*Check:* `make typecheck`.

### TYP-2 MUST

Use modern syntax: `X | None`, builtin generics, `collections.abc` for abstract containers, PEP 695 generics and
`type` aliases.

*Check:* ruff UP.

### TYP-3 MUST

While `requires-python` is below 3.14, every module starts with `from __future__ import annotations`. From 3.14 on it
is never used: [PEP 649](https://peps.python.org/pep-0649/) makes annotations lazy, and
[PEP 749](https://peps.python.org/pep-0749/) schedules the import for deprecation.

*Check:* ruff I002 with `required-imports`, set by the template only for Python below 3.14.

### TYP-4 MUST

pydantic is only for data parsed from outside: configs, HTTP bodies, files. Every other class is an attrs class:
`@frozen` for values, `@define` for stateful objects, family bases and items included. Exceptions, factories (classes
that are never instantiated) and subclasses of third-party classes stay plain classes. Classes have no hand-written
`__init__`. Construction logic goes into a classmethod constructor, or into `__attrs_post_init__` when it only derives
private state.

```python
# Bad: construction does work in __init__.
class RateLimiter:
    def __init__(self, rpm: float | None) -> None:
        self.interval_s = 60.0 / rpm if rpm else 0.0
        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()


# Good: fields declare state; a named constructor derives it.
@define
class RateLimiter:
    """Spacing between requests to one upstream."""

    interval_s: float
    _lock: asyncio.Lock = field(factory=asyncio.Lock, init=False)

    @classmethod
    def per_minute(cls, rpm: float | None) -> RateLimiter:
        return cls(60.0 / rpm if rpm else 0.0)
```

*Why:* validation libraries belong at the boundary; inside, a class should only hold already-valid data
([attrs](https://www.attrs.org/en/stable/why.html), [Hynek](https://speakerdeck.com/hynek/design-pressure)).

*Check:* `check-conventions` flags a hand-written `__init__` and dataclasses; review for pydantic inside the boundary.

### TYP-5 MUST

Mind three attrs behaviours, each verified on attrs 26.1:

- `@define` builds a new class, so a registering decorator must be the outermost one
  ([FAM-2](https://github.com/nuinashco/nuikit/blob/main/docs/guide.md#fam-2-must)).
- `__init_subclass__` runs twice for slotted classes, so hooks in it must be idempotent.
- Slots stop attribute typos only when every base class is slotted, which is why family bases are attrs classes too.

*Check:* `nuikit` registry tests.

### TYP-6 MUST

Family bases are ABCs: the registry checks subclassing, and items inherit `Config` and helpers. An injected
collaborator that only needs a shape (a clock, an HTTP client, an uploader) is typed as a `Protocol`, so fakes need no
inheritance.

*Why:* [Hynek, "Subclassing in Python Redux"](https://hynek.me/articles/python-subclassing-redux/).

*Check:* review.

### TYP-7 SHOULD

Use `Literal` for small closed sets of config values, and `StrEnum` when code iterates over the set or attaches
behaviour to it.

*Check:* review.

### TYP-8 SHOULD

Avoid `Any` outside JSON-shaped payloads and lazily imported third-party objects. Use `object` for "accepts anything".

*Check:* review.

### TYP-9 MUST

Dicts are for wire payloads only (JSON in, JSON out). A dict with a fixed set of known keys is a class.

*Check:* review.

## 4. Code style (STY)

### STY-1 MUST

Format with ruff format: 88 columns, double quotes.

*Why:* the ecosystem default, the most readable side by side, and inside the accessibility limit Black documents
([Black](https://black.readthedocs.io/en/stable/the_black_code_style/current_style.html)).

*Check:* `ruff format --check`.

### STY-2 MUST

Lint with the template's curated rule set: `E F W I B UP SIM RET PTH C4 RUF TID FBT N PERF G LOG BLE PL D NPY ERA T20
C90` (plus `FA` below 3.14). `D401` is selected explicitly, because the google docstring convention silently drops it.
Ignored on purpose: `PLR2004`, `PLR0913`, `PLC0415`, `D102`, `D103`, `D105`, `D106`, `D107`. The set changes only by
changing this guide. A `# noqa` names the rule and gives a reason.

*Why:* an explicit select keeps upgrades from changing the rules silently ([ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/linter/)).

*Check:* `ruff check`.

### STY-3 MUST

Imports are absolute.

*Check:* ruff TID252 with `ban-relative-imports = "all"`.

### STY-4 MUST

Every optional parameter and every boolean parameter is keyword-only (after `*`). Only the one or two obvious subjects
of a call are positional.

*Check:* ruff FBT for booleans; `check-conventions` flags a positional parameter with a default; review for the rest.

### STY-5 MUST

Naming:

- Modules are short nouns (`harness`, `soundness`). Functions are verbs (`select`, `bind`).
- Classes are nouns, and family items carry the family suffix (`LiteLLMEndpoint`, `GoldPatches`).
- Schemas end in `Config`. Acronyms stay capitalised (`HDBSCANClustering`, `BQ2GCSCollector`).
- Constants are UPPER_SNAKE right after the imports.
- Anything not used outside its module starts with `_`.

*Check:* ruff N; review.

### STY-6 MUST

A name holding a number with a unit ends in a short unit suffix: `_s`, `_ms`, `_mb`, `_gb`, `_tokens`, `_steps`.
Minutes and hours are spelled out (`_minutes`, `_hours`), because `_min` reads as "minimum". A name that mirrors an
external format (a file another tool reads, a library's parameters, a CLI flag) keeps that format's spelling:
`timeout_seconds` in a scorer's config file, `max_model_len` from vLLM.

*Check:* review.

### STY-7 MUST

Use pathlib, never `os.path`.

*Check:* ruff PTH.

### STY-8 MUST

`.py` files are ASCII: use `;`, `:`, `-` and `->`, never em dashes or Unicode arrows. Markdown may use any typography.

*Why:* greppable and terminal-safe.

*Check:* a pre-commit non-ASCII hook (`ascii-only-python` in the template).

### STY-9 SHOULD

Prefer early returns to nesting, comprehensions to `map`/`filter`, and `match` for dispatch on a shape or a file
suffix.

*Check:* review.

### STY-10 SHOULD

Keep within the complexity budget (C901 at 10, pylint's branch and statement limits). Split long functions at real
seams, not into one-call helpers that are shallow modules
([Ousterhout](https://github.com/johnousterhout/aposd-vs-clean-code)).

*Check:* ruff C901, PLR0912, PLR0915.

## 5. Comments and docstrings (DOC)

### DOC-1 MUST

Every module starts with a one-line docstring stating its single responsibility. A CLI module's or script's docstring
is its `--help` text and may add a usage block.

*Why:* "what is this file for" stays answerable and greppable, and keeps each module honest about its scope
([PEP 257](https://peps.python.org/pep-0257/)).

*Check:* ruff D100, D104.

### DOC-2 MUST

Docstrings are one line where possible:

- a function's is imperative ("Return the run directory for `name`."); `D401` checks this;
- a class's is a noun phrase saying what an instance represents ("Spacing between requests to one upstream.");
- every public class has one (`D101`);
- a function or method gets one when its name and signature don't already say it all.

*Check:* ruff D101, D401; `check-comments` flags a class docstring that opens with an order; review.

### DOC-3 SHOULD

Add Google-style `Args:`, `Returns:` or `Raises:` sections only for what types can't express: units, shapes, valid
ranges, what `None` or an empty value means, and errors that are part of the contract.

*Check:* review.

### DOC-4 MUST

A comment explains what the code can't say:

- an external constraint;
- a non-obvious reason;
- a unit;
- where a value came from (cite the source);
- what `None` means.

Never restate the code, never use section banners, and never leave commented-out code.

```python
# Bad: restates the code.
# Perform clustering
labels = model.fit_predict(embeddings)

# Good: says what the code can't.
# Wildcard is mandatory: BigQuery extract rejects single-file URIs for tables over 1 GB.
uri = f"{workdir_uri}/part-*.parquet"
```

*Why:* "Comments that contradict the code are worse than no comments" ([PEP 8](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/)).
Information that code can't express still needs writing down
([Ousterhout](https://github.com/johnousterhout/aposd-vs-clean-code)).

*Check:* ruff ERA001; `check-comments` flags banners; `review-comments` asks Claude whether new comments say anything
the code doesn't (the plugin's `Stop` hook, and on demand with `pre-commit run review-comments --hook-stage manual`).

### DOC-5 MUST

Comments are sentences: capitalised and ending with a period. A sentence that opens with a lowercase name puts it in
backticks (`` `git` is not installed. ``).

*Check:* `check-comments`, in pre-commit and as a Claude Code `PostToolUse` hook on every edited `.py` file.

### DOC-6 SHOULD

A `TODO` says why it isn't done now. Code generated without review is marked as such until reviewed.

*Check:* ruff TD004 to TD007 (a `TODO:` with a description); review for the why.

### DOC-7 MUST

A YAML comment, and so a `Field` description that a mirror turns into one
([CFG-3](https://github.com/nuinashco/nuikit/blob/main/docs/guide.md#cfg-3-must)), lists a setting's options
(`auto|console|json`) or says what its key and value can't: a unit the name lacks, what `null` or an edge value means,
a side effect, a source. It never repeats the key: `wandb_project: x  # W&B project` says nothing.

*Why:* when every line has a comment, readers skip them all and the few that matter go unread; DOC-4, applied to
configs.

*Check:* `review-comments` on new descriptions; the `descriptions-judge` subagent, which checks each one against the
code.

## 6. Errors (ERR)

ERR-1 and ERR-2, the `UserError` family with its exit codes and the one `@cli_boundary` per entry point, are rules of
[nuikit](https://github.com/nuinashco/nuikit/blob/main/docs/guide.md).

### ERR-3 MUST

A message is lowercase with no trailing period. It states what is wrong, then `; ` and the remedy, naming the command or
config key. An unknown name lists the valid ones.

```text
error: no soundness data; run `g4swe-grade controls` first
error: unknown endpoint kind 'gemni'; registered: gemini, litellm, passthrough
```

*Check:* `check-conventions` flags a capitalised first word and a trailing period; review for the remedy.

### ERR-4 MUST

Fail fast at the edge: check that paths exist, kinds are registered and credentials work (a one-token ping) before any
expensive work starts.

*Why:* [Shore, "Fail Fast"](https://www.martinfowler.com/ieeeSoftware/failFast.pdf).

*Check:* review.

### ERR-5 MUST

Translating an exception uses `raise ... from err`. A broad `except Exception` exists only at an isolation point, such
as a callback that must not stop training or a best-effort notification, and its `noqa` says why.

*Check:* ruff B904, BLE001.

### ERR-6 MAY

Messages are written at the raise site. Ruff's TRY003 and EM rules, which want them inside the class, are not selected.

*Check:* the rule set of STY-2 leaves out TRY003 and EM.

## 7. Logging (LOG)

LOG-1 and LOG-3, structlog over the standard library and its renderer, are rules of
[nuikit](https://github.com/nuinashco/nuikit/blob/main/docs/guide.md), whose `configure_logging` sets both up.

### LOG-2 MUST

Events are stable snake_case ids with key-value context: `log.info("proxy_started", port=8000)`. Never build an event
with an f-string or `%`.

*Why:* events stay queryable in JSON logs and in BigQuery.

*Check:* `check-conventions` flags formatted events and events that are not snake_case.

### LOG-4 MUST

Logs record events. Output meant for the user (tables, results) goes to stdout through `click.echo` or rich, never
through the logger. Library code never calls `print`.

*Check:* ruff T201, allowed only in `cli/` and `scripts/`.

### LOG-5 SHOULD

Bind run context once with `structlog.contextvars.bind_contextvars(run=...)` instead of repeating it in every event.

*Check:* review.

## 8. Tests (TST)

TST-5, the invariant tests every rnd project carries, is a rule of
[nuinashco/rnd-template](https://github.com/nuinashco/rnd-template).

### TST-1 MUST

Tests are pytest functions (no test classes) named as sentences stating a behaviour:
`test_sound_selection_never_falls_back_to_every_task`.

*Check:* `check-conventions` flags test classes; review for the names.

### TST-2 MUST

Unit tests come first. Each case covers a distinct branch or behaviour: no cross-product parametrisation, and nothing
re-tested at a higher level that a unit test already covers.

*Why:* test behaviour, one test per behaviour ([SWE at Google ch. 12](https://abseil.io/resources/swe-book/html/ch12.html)).

*Check:* review.

### TST-3 MUST

Test doubles are in-process fakes (`ScriptedEndpoint`, `httpx.MockTransport`), `tmp_path` and `monkeypatch`.
`unittest.mock` is banned. Fakes live in `tests/conftest.py` or `tests/fakes.py`; a fake with logic has its own tests.

*Why:* prefer real objects, then fakes; interaction testing couples tests to the implementation
([SWE at Google ch. 13](https://abseil.io/resources/swe-book/html/ch13.html),
[Fowler](https://martinfowler.com/articles/mocksArentStubs.html)).

*Check:* ruff `banned-api`.

### TST-4 MUST

The layout mirrors `src/` module by module: `tests/<pkg>/<sub>/test_<module>.py` for every module with branching logic.
Exempt modules are those with nothing a unit test could distinguish: schemas whose rules pydantic enforces, error
classes, re-exporting `__init__` files, and thin wrappers that only start an external process (a `docker build`). They
are covered by the invariants or the integration test. Cross-cutting invariants live in `tests/test_invariants.py`.
End-to-end tests live in `tests/integration/`, are marked `integration` and are deselected by default
(`-m integration` runs them).

*Check:* `--strict-markers`; review.

### TST-6 MUST

Child processes, servers and Docker appear only in tests of what can't be measured in process. Before adding a slow
test, check `pytest --durations=10`. The unit suite stays under about 10 s.

*Check:* review.

### TST-7 SHOULD

Separate arrange, act and assert with blank lines. Compare related values in one tuple assert. A test module's
docstring states the invariant it protects.

*Check:* review.

### TST-8 SHOULD

Test ML code with tiny real models, not mocks: loss decreases, and a batch can be overfitted
([Yan](https://eugeneyan.com/writing/unit-testing-ml/)).

*Check:* review.

## 9. Repository docs (RDOC)

### RDOC-1 MUST

README.md is the user's and operator's view: setup, daily workflow, commands, outputs, caveats. CONTRIBUTING.md is the
contributor's view: architecture, layout, families, configs, deviations, the "Extending" table, tests and commits.

*Why:* one document, one purpose ([SWE at Google ch. 10](https://abseil.io/resources/swe-book/html/ch10.html)).

*Check:* template skeletons.

### RDOC-2 MUST

A standalone subpackage has its own README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md next to its code.

*Check:* review.

### RDOC-3 MUST

Diagrams are mermaid. Flowcharts colour pure components with `classDef pure` and effectful ones with `classDef side`,
using the template's palette. The main run gets one sequence diagram.

*Check:* template.

### RDOC-4 MUST

AGENTS.md is the entry point for coding agents, at most 60 lines: commands, layout, what this repo asks beyond the
conventions, and pointers to CONTRIBUTING. CLAUDE.md is `@AGENTS.md`, plus any Claude-only extras. The conventions
reach Claude through the `conventions` plugin of the `nuinashco` marketplace (its skills, its `conventions-reviewer`
and `descriptions-judge` subagents and its hooks, TOOL-4), and a project's own path-scoped rules live in
`.claude/rules/`. Agent files never copy this guide, and leave to linters what linters check.

*Why:* [agents.md](https://agents.md/); [Claude Code memory](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) recommends short,
specific files, and a skill or a path-scoped rule loads only when its files are in play.

*Check:* template; review.

### RDOC-5 MUST

Docs change in the same commit as the code they describe. A stale doc is a bug.

*Check:* review.

## 10. Git (GIT)

### GIT-1 MUST

Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/):

- a standard type: `feat fix docs refactor test build ci perf style chore revert`;
- an optional scope;
- a lowercase imperative subject, with no period, of at most 72 characters;
- no articles (`a`, `an`, `the`) and no filler: say what changed in as few words as hold it.

Example: `fix(proxy): retry on 429 from upstream`, not `fix(proxy): add a retry for the 429 errors`.

*Why:* the default tooling accepts exactly these types, and the imperative matches git's own convention
([Beams](https://cbea.ms/git-commit/)).

*Check:* the `conventional-pre-commit` and `check-commit-msg` commit-msg hooks.

### GIT-2 MUST

A commit message is one line: no body and no trailers. A reason worth keeping goes where readers look for it: a code
comment for a constraint, the PR description for an alternative that was rejected. Claude Code's own trailer is off in
`.claude/settings.json` (`attribution`).

*Check:* `check-commit-msg`.

### GIT-3 MUST

Branches are short-lived and named `<type>/<slug>` (`feat/`, `fix/`, `docs/`, `refactor/`, plus `exp/` for
experiments). Merges are squash-merges, and the PR title is the conventional commit that lands on `main`. `make github`
sets the repo up once: squash-merge only, the PR title as the commit title with an empty body (GIT-2), merged branches
deleted. GitHub appends ` (#N)` to the title, so PR titles stay within 65 characters.

*Check:* `make github`; review.

### GIT-5 MUST

Secrets, data, run outputs and notebook outputs are never committed.

*Check:* gitleaks, nbstripout, `.gitignore`.

### GIT-6 MUST

A PR description follows `.github/pull_request_template.md`: a summary of why, the changes made with the alternatives
rejected, and the checklist; results, how to reproduce them and notes for the reviewer when they apply.

*Why:* commits are one line, so the PR holds the reasoning, and the squash commit links to it by number.

*Check:* template; review.

## 11. Tooling (TOOL)

TOOL-3, keeping a generated project on its template with `copier update`, is a rule of
[nuinashco/rnd-template](https://github.com/nuinashco/rnd-template).

### TOOL-1 MUST

`make check` runs ruff check, ruff format `--check`, pyright, `lint-imports` and pytest, and CI runs it on every pull
request. pre-commit runs the fast checks plus the commit-msg lint, nbstripout, gitleaks and the `uv lock` check.

*Why:* rules that a tool can check are enforced by a tool
([SWE at Google ch. 8](https://abseil.io/resources/swe-book/html/ch08.html)).

*Check:* template.

### TOOL-2 MUST

Tool versions come from `uv.lock`. Hooks for Python tools are local `uv run` hooks, so pre-commit, CI and editors all
use the same versions.

*Check:* template.

### TOOL-4 MUST

The checks this guide adds on top of ruff are the `conventions-hooks` package of nuinashco/conventions. A repo opts in
with a `[tool.conventions]` table in its root `pyproject.toml`, where `ignore = ["STY-4"]` turns rules off for that
repo, and adds the package as a dev dependency pinned by `uv.lock`. The package's commands are `check-comments`,
`check-conventions`, `check-protected`, `check-commit-msg` and `review-comments`. The checks run in two layers with the
same code: pre-commit gates every commit by anyone, and the `conventions` Claude Code plugin gives Claude the findings
while it works (`PreToolUse` before an edit, `PostToolUse` after it, `Stop` before it hands back). The plugin runs the
project's own `.venv/bin/<command>`, so each project gets the version its lock pins, and does nothing in a repo that has
not opted in.

*Why:* only pre-commit sees every author, but feedback during the edit is cheaper than at commit time. One plugin,
enabled once per machine, serves every repo without copying hook settings into each.

*Check:* template; the opt-in and plugin tests of nuinashco/conventions.

### TOOL-5 MUST

Files nobody edits by hand are listed in `.gitattributes` with `protected=<why>`:

- `generated`: config mirrors, `.copier-answers.yml`, and whatever a build step writes;
- `vendored`: code copied in from another repo and changed only there;
- `published`: third-party files kept as published, such as `notebooks/reference/`.

The same lines carry `linguist-generated` or `linguist-vendored`, so GitHub folds those diffs in pull requests. A
family item's mirror sits beside hand-written presets, so no path pattern can mark it: a leading comment line starting
`# Generated by` marks it instead. The `check-protected` Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook refuses edits to all of them with
the reason and the right place to make the change; the commands that own them (`make configs`, `copier update`) still
write them. The hook fails open: a broken environment lets edits through instead of blocking every one. Names carry
no marker (no `_` prefix): `_` means private in Python.

*Why:* agents fix whatever file is in front of them, and a refusal that names the source is the cheapest redirect.

*Check:* template; `check-protected PATH`.

### TOOL-6 SHOULD

A check that asks an LLM, such as a `claude -p` hook or a review subagent, is a judge and is built as one: narrow
criteria with named verdicts, an "unsure" outcome instead of a guess, a cited line for every finding, a fresh context
holding only the artefact and the rules, and structured output wherever code reads the verdict. It has a labelled set
of passing and failing cases, rerun whenever its prompt or model changes; every error it makes becomes a case. Anything
a script can decide stays a script.

*Why:* a judge's leniency or harshness shows only against labelled cases, and a narrow, cited criterion is easier to
align than a broad rubric ([Husain](https://hamel.dev/blog/posts/llm-judge/),
[Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents)).

*Check:* review; the plugin's judges are measured by `make test-judges` in nuinashco/conventions.

## Decisions

Contested choices, what was weighed and why this guide picks what it does. Revisit an entry when its reason no longer
holds. The choices behind the shared library (families, the config bridge, config defaults, errors, logging) are in
[nuikit's guide](https://github.com/nuinashco/nuikit/blob/main/docs/guide.md), and those behind the project layout in
[nuinashco/rnd-template](https://github.com/nuinashco/rnd-template).

| topic | decision | alternatives | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| line length | 88 | 79 (PEP 8, Google), 100, 120 (earlier repos) | ecosystem default; no primary guide endorses 120 |
| multi-part repos | one package with subpackages | uv workspace; several top-level modules | simplest, no name clashes; import-linter keeps the boundaries |
| shared building blocks | the `nuikit` library, a dependency pinned by `uv.lock` | vendored by the template; copying by hand | one source with its own tags; a project takes a fix by upgrading one dependency, not by a template update |
| rules for agents | written once in `rules/`, generated into this guide and the `conventions` plugin's skills and subagents | a copy of the guide in every project; hand-kept agent files | one source; every repo gets a new rule through the plugin, and Claude loads only the area it works in |
| config comments | only options and what the key can't say | a description on every field | comments that repeat the key bury the ones that matter |
| data classes | attrs for every class, pydantic for configs | dataclasses; pydantic everywhere | validation at the edge, plain typed state inside; no `__init__` boilerplate |
| interfaces | ABC families, Protocol seams | ABC only; Protocol only | registries need nominal bases; fakes need none |
| type checker | pyright standard, strict on libraries such as `nuikit` | mypy --strict; basedpyright; ty (beta) | checks unannotated code; understands attrs and pydantic natively |
| `__future__` annotations | always below 3.14, never from 3.14 | never; only where needed | consistent and automatic; follows PEP 649/749 |
| module docstrings | one line on every module | only `__init__` and CLI (earlier rule) | each module states its responsibility (PEP 257, Google) |
| test doubles | fakes, mocks banned | mocks at unmanaged edges (Khorikov) | tests don't couple to the implementation (SWE at Google ch. 13) |
| commits | standard types, imperative, one line, no articles | custom `doc`/`ref`; behaviour-as-fact subjects; bodies with the why | default tooling accepts them; git convention; terse history you can scan |
| merging | squash | rebase-merge; commit to main | messy branch history is fine; `main` stays one commit per change |
| Python | latest stable | 3.12 floor | newest language features; pin lower per project when forced |
